FOREWORD This lndian Standard (Part 5) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Marine Instruments and Safety Aids Sectional Committee had been approved by the Transport Engineering Division Council. Pyrotechnic distress signal form parts of the lifeboats and liferafts equipment in accordance with LiJe Rules, 3936 under the Me~hrrnl Shipping Act, 1958.

SavingApplimces

The Indian Standards covering the whole range of pyrotechnic distress signals are being published in the following parts: Shipbuilding-Pyrotechnic distress signals for ships : Part 1 General requirements Part 2 Red flare parachute signal Part 3 Red star rocket signal Part 4 White flare signal Part 6 Explosive shell signal Part 7 Explosive rocket signal Part S Orange smoke signal Part 9 Red flare signal These standards are based on GB 3107.1-3107.9-1952 by the China State Bureau of Standard. `Standards of pyrotechnic signals for ships, issued

The Composition of the Committee responsible for the preparation of this standard is given in Annex A. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

SHIPBUILDING-PYROTECHNIC SIGNALS FOR SHIPS
PART 5 WHITE FLARE PARACHUTE SIGNAL -

DISTRESS

SPECIFICATION

1 SCOPE This standard (Part 5) specifics sizes, materials and tests for white flare parachute signals for use in ships communication among the rcscuc station, Marine cmergcncy help unirs and distress ships and people or for illumination required for search and rcscuc operations. Its pcrformancc conforms to the stipulations of SOLAS Convention 1974. 2 REFERENCE IS 14270 (Part 1) : 1995 `Shipbuilding Pyrotechnic distress signals for ships : Part 1 Gcner~11requircmcnts', is ncccssary adjunct to this standard.
3 `II~RiVIINOLOGY

5.2 After this signal is ignited either by pulling or by striking, it shall be ejcctcd into the air using rockets to a height of not less than 300 m, to give out white flare hanging by parachute, its flare shall have: a strength of not less than 15 000 candela (cd). b) a duration of not less than 60 seconds. c) white colour according to the diagam stipulated by International Illumination Committee. Area limit of its chromaticity shall be within the scope of the following coordinates : -__ __-___ X 0.525 0.525 0.452 0.310 0.310 0.443 Y 0.3S2 0.440 0.440 0.348 0.253 0.352 ____ d) a descending speed of not more than 5 m/s. The white flare shall also not burn the parachute and accessories. of small ignition diameter less than a)

For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in IS 14270 (Part 1) : 1995, shall apply. 4 I~ORM AND SIZE 4.1 White flare parachute signal for ships is the rocket driven flame type pyrotechnicsignal, ignited either by pulling or by striking. Its main componcnts include: a) b) c) d) e) f) 2) Rocket launcher and rocket body, Signal chemical sticks, Parachute and accessories, Ignition device, Shell and guiding tube, Connecting item, and Safety cap and top cap.

5.3 Signal chemical stick shall be made grains of black chemical, gun powder, chemical, signal chemical, etc. Its outer shall be 35 to 37 mm, weight shall not bc 70 3.

5.4 Parachute body shall be of rectangular or round shape, its size shall conform to the rcquircmcnts of 4.2 of this standard, chute thread shall have sufficient strength, signal sticks shall bc hanged to one end by using 300 mm long thin steel wire or chain. 5.5. Rocket launcher is made up of rocket body, gun powder, propellant and outer shell. Outer shell is aluminium tube of outer diameter not less than 35 mm, the diameter of the nozzle of the steel rocket body shall bc suitable for the propellant, on the upper surface of the rocket body the signal chemical sticks and parachute signals are placed. 5.6 Ignition device shall conform to the stipulations of 4.1 of IS 14270 (Part 1 ) : 1995. 5.7 She11 and direction tube shall be made of plastic or equivalent material.

4.2 The outer diameter of the white flare parachute signal for ship shall not exceed 45 mm, and total length shall not be more than 290 mm. Its total weight shall not exceed 450 2. 5 CONSTRUCTION ANI) GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 5.1 White flare parachute signal for ships shall conform to 1s 14270 (Part 1) : 1995.

IS 14270(Part 5) : 1997
5.8 Connecting item is made of plastic or equivalent material. Its one end is connected to the signal shell and the other to the safety cap. A=

s=

5.9 Safety cap and the top may be made of plastic or metal, its height shall not be more than 25 mm, its outer surface shall have knurling and be red in colour. Metal caps shall undergo anticorrosive treatment. 5.10 The outer shape and composition of this signal shall conform to the stipulations of 4.2 of IS 14270 (Part 1) : 1995. 5.11 The signal, in release condition without the safety cap, shall be immersed in 10 cm deep water for one minute and its utility performance shall not be affected. 5.12 When subjected to a salt spray (20 percent natrium chloride solution) at a temperature of 35+3"C for at least 100 h the signal shall function effectively. 5.13 The signal, while igniting shall not have any blind fire, explosion or mishap. Rocket shall be safe and dependable, its initial thrust shall be adequate and the igniting flame shall not burn the hand of the person releasing it. 5.14 The signal, when freely dropped on a steel sheet from a height of 3 m shall not ignite or explode and its utility performance shall not be affected by the impact. 5.15 The test for the validity period of the signal shall conform to the stipulations of 6.4 of IS 14270 (Part 1) : 1995. 6 TESTING 6.1 Test methods of the signal shall conform to the stipulations of IS 14270 (Part 1) : 1995 6.2 Flare Strength and Duration Test 6.2.1 Determination of the flare strength shall be done by using `ST' type or equivalent lux meter, under the test lab conditions of simulated black body and wind speed of 5 m/s. It shall be started at the 5th second after igniting; reading 5 values at an interval of 5 seconds and after calculating its average, the result shall be arrived at as per the following formula :
I =AS*

luminous intensity of light source perpendicular to lux-meter, Lu;and distance of the lux meter from the light source, nt.

6.2.2 Flame duration time is determined by stop watch when measuring the flare strength. Its duration is calculated from starting of the flame till it has died out. During release test also, the flame duration time shall be noted down for comparison. 6.2.3 The flare strength and flare duration of each batch of products is taken separately to calculate the average value of each test samples. 6.3 Flare Chromaticity Test Flare chromaticity is measured by using calorimeter in the flare chromaticity area limit or under the sunlight by the measurement method, using human eyes in which standard white colour sample plates, as per the stipulations of 5.2 of this standard, are compared with its colour. This test may be conducted simultaneously with the flare strength measurement. 6.4 Launching Height Test The height of the rocket launched is measured at the test field or at the time of release on ship, by using height measuring equipment. Its height is measured from the launching place to the place where parachute and white flame are just stationary. 6.5 Release Test Release test may be conducted on the special launcher, but at least one signal shall be hand released. 6.6 Vibration test, dropping test, test, high temperature test and mance test of the signal shall stipulations of 5.2 to 5.5 and (Part 1) : 1995. 7 INSI~ECTION 7.1 Product inspection of the signal shall conform to the stipulations of 6.1 to 6.4 of IS 14270 (Part 1) : 1995 7.2 Items, scope and the quantity of selected samples in each group for the delivery inspection of the signal shall conforrrI to the stipulations given in Table 1. low temperature general pcrforconform to the 5.8 of IS 14270

llureau of Indian Standards

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indimz Standards Act, 1986 to promotc harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country.
Copyright

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of ncccssary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS.
Review of Indian Standards

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes arc ncedcd, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and `Standards: Monthly Additions'. This Indian Standard has been developed from Dot : No. TED 20 ( 963 ).
